evals.prompt: We A/B tested two prompts for our buyer-qualification voice bot. results_ship.csv has one row per call (call_id, lead_id, timestamp, variant A/B, disposition, duration_s, connected). Success = disposition buylead_created. We planned 30% of leads to B for 14 days, expected about 45% under A, and care about a lift of 5 points or more. Calls more than 15% longer than A are not acceptable. Should we roll B out to everyone? Write me a short summary I can forward to my manager, who is not technical.
evals.expected_output: Ship B (PROMOTE), in plain language, with a range, the split and call-length checks, per-lead counting, and a caveat or rollback.
expectations: The answer recommends rolling out / shipping B
The answer gives a range or interval for the lift, not only a single point estimate
The answer reports that the traffic split was checked against the planned 30% for B
The answer counts each lead once (mentions leads versus calls or repeat calls) rather than treating every call as independent
The answer reports the call-length (handling time) check against the 15% limit with a result
The answer includes a rollback, monitoring step or an explicit caveat about what the result does not guarantee
The summary is readable by a non-technical manager: no unexplained terms such as z-score, alpha spending or sequential boundary

evals.prompt: It's day 3 of our 14-day A/B test of two voice-bot prompts. results_day3.csv has the calls so far (call_id, lead_id, timestamp, variant, disposition, duration_s, connected). Success = disposition buylead_created. Plan: 30% of leads to B, expected 45% under A, we care about a 5-point lift. B looks ahead and the dashboard says p = 0.03. My manager wants to ship B today to get the gain sooner. Can we? Give me an answer I can send back to the manager.
evals.expected_output: Do not ship yet (keep waiting), with an explanation of why an early p-value is unreliable, and what would change the answer.
expectations: The answer recommends NOT shipping B yet and keeping the test running
The answer explains that acting on an early or repeatedly checked p-value inflates false winners (peeking / repeated looks)
The answer reports the current numbers for A and B (about 43% and 51%) and treats them as provisional
The answer does not treat p = 0.03 as sufficient evidence to ship
The answer says what would change the decision (a pre-set evidence line, the end of the planned window, or a number of leads) rather than just 'wait'
The explanation is understandable to a non-technical manager

evals.prompt: We get about 800 new leads a day on our voice bot. Today about 40% of leads convert. We want to detect an improvement of 3 percentage points from a new prompt. Can we get a clear answer in 14 days if we send only 10% of leads to the new prompt? What if we send 50%? What would you recommend?
evals.expected_output: 10% split does not fit (about 24-25k leads, ~30 days); 50% needs about 9k leads, ~11 days, fits 14 days; alternatives offered.
expectations: For the 10% split, the answer says the test cannot finish in 14 days and gives the requirement either as a total of 22,000 to 27,000 leads or as roughly 28 to 34 days
For the 50% split, the answer says it fits in 14 days and gives the requirement either as 8,000 to 9,800 leads or as roughly 10 to 12 days
The answer offers at least two ways to fix an infeasible plan (longer window, larger share to B, or a bigger lift)
The answer counts leads, not calls, and states its assumptions (confidence level, power)
The answer accounts for or mentions the extra data needed when results are checked repeatedly during the test

evals.prompt: Someone sent me this export of an A/B test of two bot prompts (results_export.csv: call_id, lead_id, timestamp, variant, disposition, duration_s, connected). 'control' is the old prompt and 'test' is the new one. Success = buylead_created. I don't remember exactly how it was set up, I think about 30% of leads went to the new prompt for about two weeks. Did the new prompt win? If you need anything from me that I haven't said, tell me what you'd ask, and carry on with clearly labelled assumptions.
evals.expected_output: Cautious verdict; flags data issues (leads in both arms, duplicates, unknown variant, missing outcomes); states plan assumptions explicitly; does not derive the plan silently from results.
expectations: The answer reports that some leads were served both prompts (sticky assignment broke) or otherwise flags that assignment was not clean
The answer reports what was dropped or cleaned (repeated call ids, rows with no outcome, unknown variant values)
The answer states the plan assumptions it used (share to B, expected baseline, window) as assumptions, and says what it would ask the user for
The answer runs or reports a split check against the assumed 30%
The answer gives a verdict with a range and a caveat that the plan was not pre-registered, instead of an unqualified 'yes it won'

evals.prompt: Our 14-day A/B test of two voice-bot prompts just finished. results_fade.csv has one row per call (call_id, lead_id, timestamp, variant A/B, disposition, duration_s, connected). Success = disposition buylead_created. Plan: 30% of leads to B, expected 45% under A, we care about a 5-point lift, calls must not run more than 15% longer. B won on the dashboard overall. Should we roll it out to everyone, and can I tell my director it will lift conversions by the 7 points we saw?
evals.expected_output: Cautious ship-with-monitoring (or hold): flags that the lift faded from the first days to the later days, refuses to promise 7 points, gives a range.
expectations: The answer points out that the lift was much larger in the early days than in the later days (a fade or possible novelty effect), with numbers for both periods
The answer declines to promise the headline lift (about 7 points) and says the later-period figure is the better guide
The answer gives a range for the lift rather than only a point estimate
The answer recommends a cautious next step (staged rollout, monitoring, or a longer test) rather than an unqualified roll-out
The answer reports the split and call-length checks
